work.permit: Autorización del Secretario del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos

note: Majority: Civil Code of Puerto Rico 2020 (Law No. 55-2020), Article 97 (31 L.P.R.A. § 5591), read in the copy the Office of Management and Budget's library publishes: everyone comes of age at 21, and from then has full capacity for all civil acts; the code's statement of motives says the age stays at 21. Emancipation (by marriage or concession) isn't held. Work: Law No. 230 of 12 May 1942, as amended (Minors' Employment Law), Article 2 (29 L.P.R.A. § 432), read in the Department of Labour and Human Resources' library: no minor under 16 may be employed in any gainful occupation, except that minors of 14 to 16 may work outside school hours and in school holidays in occupations the law doesn't forbid; every minor's employment needs the Department's employment permit (the Department's page on minors' permits says so), which the form doesn't hold for those of 16 and 17. Law No. 112 of 1985 (29 L.P.R.A. § 475 ff.) lets minors under 14 be hired or used in artistic work or show business (musicians, dancers, singers and the like) only with the prior authorisation of the Secretary of Labour and Human Resources, on the terms he sets, under Regulation No. 3479 of 12 March 1987 (not read); no lower age is set. Performers of 14 and 15 come under Law 230's permit. Service: Puerto Rico is under the United States' Selective Service: the Selective Service System says almost all male US citizens and male immigrants aged 18 through 25 must register, that registration is not enlisting, and that there is no draft; so service is none, and the registration duty is in this note.

sources.title: Oficina de Gerencia y Presupuesto, Biblioteca Virtual: Código Civil de Puerto Rico de 2020 (Ley Núm. 55-2020)
sources.said: Artículo 97. — Mayoría de edad. (31 L.P.R.A. § 5591) Toda persona adviene a la mayoría de edad cuando cumple veintiún (21) años. Desde entonces tiene plena capacidad para realizar por si misma todos los actos civiles

sources.title: Departamento del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos, Ley Núm. 230 de 1942, Ley de Empleo de Menores
sources.said: Ningún menor de dieciséis (16) años de edad será empleado ni se le permitirá ni tolerará que trabaje en Puerto Rico en ninguna ocupación lucrativa, ni en relación con ella; Disponiéndose, que menores entre catorce (14) y menos de dieciséis (16) años podrán ser empleados, fuera de horas de clase y durante las vacaciones escolares

sources.title: Departamento del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos, Ley Núm. 112 de 1985, Ley de Empleo de Menores de 14 Años o Menos en Actividades Artísticas
sources.said: se podrá contratar o utilizar, previa autorización del Secretario del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos, a menores de catorce (14) años, para trabajar o dedicarse a actividades artísticas o a actividades propias del género del espectáculo

sources.title: Departamento del Trabajo y Recursos Humanos, Negociado de Normas del Trabajo
sources.said: Los permisos de empleo de menores se otorgan de acuerdo a las disposiciones de la Ley Núm. 230 de 1942, según enmendada.

sources.title: Selective Service System, Who Needs to Register
sources.said: Almost all male US citizens and male immigrants, who are 18 through 25, are required to register with Selective Service.

sources.title: Selective Service System, home page
sources.said: Registration is not the same as enlisting with the U.S. Armed Forces. There is no draft and registration does not mean automatic induction into the military.
